newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks ignore gloomy jobs data,dlr rises.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks ignore gloomy jobs data,dlr rises.

text.p: Rising German unemployment figures, showing economic growth too weak to revive the country's job prospects, sent the dollar to five week highs against the mark on Friday.
German shares shrugged off the gloomy news, however, and hit a new trading peak, while the London stock market appeared to take a quarter point rise in interest rates in its stride.
Wall Street's firm perfomance overnight provided European bourses with a good start to the day, but financial markets were waiting for key U.S. jobs data for May, due out at 1230 GMT.
Precious metals palladium and platinum, which have soared in recent days because of delays in Russian exports, pushed sharply higher again during the morning.
Platinum zoomed $60 to $495 an ounce to its highest level since 1990, while palladium fixed at a 17-year high of $240.00, up $30.

The dollar was raring to go after hitting five-week highs against the mark after the German jobless rise stoked doubts about European monetary union and contrasted with an expected jump in U.S. non-farm payrolls.

The German figures, which showed a seasonally adjusted rise of 56,000 in the number of people out of work to 4.358 million, intensified concerns over how Bonn could cut its budget deficit to the 3.0 percent of GDP required for the European single currency.

"The German jobless numbers are making people ask what Kohl and Waigel are going to do about their budget problems and make them more inclined to hold long dollar positions," said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered."

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and his embattled finance minister Theo Waigel have repeatedly declared their commitment to meeting strict criteria for economic and monetary unilon (EMU), despite Germany's sizeable budget shortfall.
The dollar stood at 1.7360 marks at 1115 GMT, up from late Thursday's 1.7285. Earlier it hit 1.7373, its strongest level since reaching a 1997 high of 1.7389 on April 28.
Against the yen the dollar stood at 115.73 versus 115.65, its upside capped by a report that Japan's trade surplus would be discussed at the June 20-22 Group of Seven summit in Denver.
Despite gloomy comments from German officials at the prospects of a revival in the jobs market, the country's share market remained strong although off its intraday record.
With the market still underpinned by Wall Street and the strength of the dollar, traders said the German jobless figures had little impact because some of the numbers had been leaked.
SGL Carbon was a prominent loser, down 22.2 marks at 238 on news its was cooperating with a U.S.-EU probe into graphite electrode price fixing allegations.
British shares eased from their best levels after the Bank of England raised interest rates to 6.5 percent from 6.25, but the market overall was little moved by the expected move.
By mid-session the FTSE-100 index was up 30.5 points, or 0.67 percent, at 4,606.7.

Cable & Wireless helped lead the market higher after its Hong Kong unit Hong Kong Telecom confirmed C&W was in talks with the Chinese authorities on possible co-operation. NatWest led banks upwards on a renewed bout of bid speculation, rising 35.5 pence to 772.5.
French shares rose through the 2,700 level on the blue chip CAC-40 index but were trading a little below their highs by mid-session.
Dealers cited an inflow of foreign liquidity and the the German unemployment figures as factors in the rise.
Retailer Pinault-Printemps jumped 3.82 percent to 2,638 after its general meeting on Thursday. Brokers Ferri said the group had made an excellent start to the year.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7360 marks and 115.73 yen compared with 1.7285 marks and 115.65 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 30.5 points, or 0.67 percent, at 4,606.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 23.35 points, or 0.87 percent, at 2,714.2.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 20.85 points, or 0.57 percent, at 3,693.88.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold fixed at $343.80 versus $340.80 on Thursday afternoon. Silver was 14 cents stronger at $4.94. Platinum was trading at seven-year highs after being fixed at $495.00 versus $442.00, while palladium fixed at a 17-year high of $240.00, up $30.
